entries.title: Polymer Melt Stability Monitoring in Injection Moulding Using LSTM-Based Time-Series Models
entries.machine: Fully operational industrial thermoplastic injection-moulding production line; machine identity is not relied upon for cross-site generalisation in this registry.
entries.material: Industrial thermoplastic production material or materials used on the monitored line; specific grade identity is not used as a transferable process rule.
entries.tool: Production injection mould and machine/tooling combination observed continuously during normal manufacturing.
outcomes: stable versus volatile pre-defect operating windows
entries.scale: Approximately 280,000 injection cycles collected over about six months of continuous industrial production.

raw.license: article open access; reusable industrial production rows are not confirmed public

entries.limitation: The unusually long industrial record is strong evidence for real process drift, but the volatile pre-defect labels are partly physically informed/derived around operator-identified defect events. Prediction of instability is not proof of a specific physical root cause, and the learned boundaries are site-, product-, machine-, material- and tooling-specific.

entries.title: In-cavity pressure measurements for failure diagnosis in the injection moulding process and correlation with numerical simulation
entries.journal: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
entries.machine: Ferromatik Elektra 110T injection-moulding machine with Wemo handling and Thermovan temperature-control equipment.
entries.material: Domamid 6G30 300 BK PA6-GF30 moulded in the reported overmoulding/tool-validation programme with a polypropylene/glass preparation context.
entries.tool: Instrumented production-relevant mould using Kistler Type 6157C cavity-pressure and Type 6190C pressure/temperature sensors with ComoNeo 5887A acquisition; venting and gate/tool condition were investigated.
outcomes: defect elimination or improvement after venting/tool maintenance and controlled process changes
entries.scale: Controlled experimental fault-diagnosis series with multiple cavity sensor locations and before/after process/tool interventions; exact cycle count is not used as a corpus total.

raw.license: article CC BY 4.0; reusable raw sensor traces are not confirmed as a public dataset

entries.limitation: This study is unusually valuable because it links real defects, cavity measurements, tool/venting diagnosis and corrective action, but it concerns one mould, reinforced polyamide system and machine/tool condition. The measured pressures, switch points and maintenance observations are not universal defect thresholds or production settings.

entries.title: Scientific Molding and Adaptive Process Quality Control with External Sensors for Injection Molding Process
entries.machine: Injection-moulding production/validation equipment at two independent operating sites; exact machine identities remain study-specific.
entries.material: Thermoplastic production materials used in the two-site continuous-production validation; grade-specific numerical behavior is not generalized in this registry.
entries.tool: Production moulding setups instrumented externally with a nozzle pressure sensor and tie-bar strain measurement for online quality characteristics.
signals: tie-bar strain and derived clamping-force curves
injection speed and V/P setup history
outcomes: repeatability under continuous production at two sites
entries.scale: Continuous production experiments at two sites following scientific-moulding setup and adaptive-control validation.

raw.license: article open access; reusable two-site production rows are not confirmed public

entries.limitation: Two-site continuous-production validation improves external validity compared with a single laboratory DOE, but the reported sensor features, fitted adjustments and product-weight behavior remain specific to the tested machines, moulds, materials and products. Adaptive prediction/control performance does not create universal nozzle-pressure, tie-bar-strain or process limits.

entries.title: Cavity pressure-based holding pressure adjustment for enhancing the consistency of injection molding quality
entries.machine: Controlled injection-moulding experimental system used for thin-wall specimen production; exact press identity is not required for the bounded registry claim.
entries.material: Thermoplastic material used for the thin-walled dumbbell-shaped validation specimen; grade-specific numerical settings remain study-specific.
entries.tool: Thin-walled dumbbell specimen mould instrumented for cavity-pressure measurement and shot-to-shot holding-pressure adjustment.
outcomes: quality consistency under imposed barrel-temperature change
entries.scale: Controlled disturbance-and-compensation injection-moulding experiment with repeated shot-level cavity-pressure and physical-quality measurements.

raw.license: publisher article; reusable raw shot-level data are not confirmed public

entries.limitation: The experiment demonstrates that cavity-pressure feedback can suppress quality drift caused by an imposed disturbance in the tested thin-wall moulding system. It does not establish a universal holding-pressure adjustment law, cavity-pressure target, acceptable dimensional window or causal model for unrelated machines, moulds or resins.

entries.title: Experimental investigation of plastic injection molding: Assessment of the effects of cavity pressure and mold temperature on the quality of the final products
entries.machine: Instrumented injection-moulding experimental cell using a Kistler CoMo 2869A acquisition/monitoring apparatus; the exact press identity is not used as a transferable rule.
entries.material: Thermoplastic material used in the reported experimental injection-moulding programme; study-specific material and geometry bound the numerical findings.
entries.tool: Injection mould instrumented with pressure and combined temperature-pressure sensors to record cavity pressure and mould-surface temperature.
entries.scale: Controlled experimental study relating directly measured in-cavity pressure and mould temperature to physical final-part quality.

raw.license: publisher article; reusable raw experimental rows/traces are not confirmed public

entries.limitation: This well-established experiment supports the physical importance of cavity pressure and mould temperature, but it is an older single experimental system with study-specific material, mould geometry and instrumentation. Its measured values and correlations do not establish universal pressure, mould-temperature, shrinkage or warpage limits.
